discovery: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated many-body systems with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, Germany

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

nominees.name: Ignacio Cirac
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics, Garching, Germany

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum many-body physics
motivation: Feynman's idea of simulating quantum matter with a controllable quantum system has become a working laboratory reality, chiefly through ultracold atoms in optical lattices. In 1998 Jaksch, Bruder, Cirac, Gardiner and Zoller showed that bosonic atoms in optical lattices realise the Hubbard model with tunable parameters. In 2002 Bloch and co-workers then observed the superfluid-to-Mott-insulator quantum phase transition. This opened a field in which long-standing questions of condensed-matter physics can be tested cleanly and quantitatively: Hubbard physics, antiferromagnetic correlations, many-body localisation, synthetic gauge fields and topological bands, out-of-equilibrium dynamics, and site-resolved quantum gas microscopy. Cirac and Zoller also laid much of the conceptual groundwork for controlled quantum many-body systems, including trapped-ion quantum computation. Bloch's experiments turned these ideas into a precise and versatile platform used today by laboratories around the world.
